## Big idea in one line

**Pointcuts** choose *which* methods get advice.  
**Proxy type** chooses *how* Spring wraps the bean (interface-based JDK proxy vs subclass-based CGLIB) — and that affects what can be intercepted.

```text
Pointcut expression ──► matching methods
Spring wraps bean ────► JDK proxy OR CGLIB proxy
Caller uses proxy ────► advice runs
```

***

## Topic 1 — `execution` pointcut (most common)

Shape:

```text
execution( modifiers? return-type declaring-type? method-name(params) throws? )
```

Examples:

```java
// any method in a package
execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))

// any public method named save
execution(public * save(..))

// ProductService only
execution(* com.example.demo.service.ProductService.*(..))

// one arg
execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(*))

// starts with get
execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.get*(..))
```

| Piece | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `*` return | any return type |
| `..` in params | any number of args (including 0) |
| `*` in params | exactly one arg of any type |
| `*` in name/package | wildcard segment |

***

## Topic 2 — Other useful pointcut kinds

```java
// methods annotated with @GetMapping (example)
@annotation(org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping)

// any method in classes annotated @Service
@within(org.springframework.stereotype.Service)

// bean name patterns (Spring extension)
bean(*Service)
```

You can combine with `&&`, `||`, `!`:

```java
@Around("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..)) && !execution(* com.example.demo.service.InternalService.*(..))")
```

***

## Topic 3 — Named pointcuts (cleaner aspects)

```java
@Aspect
@Component
public class TimingAspect {

    @Pointcut("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
    public void serviceLayer() {}

    @Around("serviceLayer()")
    public Object time(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
        long t = System.currentTimeMillis();
        try {
            return pjp.proceed();
        } finally {
            System.out.println(pjp.getSignature() + " " + (System.currentTimeMillis() - t) + "ms");
        }
    }
}
```

One expression, many advice methods can reuse `serviceLayer()`.

***

## Topic 4 — JDK dynamic proxy vs CGLIB

```text
Bean implements an interface?
  │
  ├─ YES (classic Spring default story)
  │     JDK dynamic proxy
  │     - implements the same interface(s)
  │     - cast to interface type works
  │     - cast to concrete class may fail
  │
  └─ NO  (class only)  OR Boot often prefers CGLIB anyway
        CGLIB proxy
        - subclass of the concrete class
        - works without an interface
```

### Practical rules

1. Prefer injecting the **interface** type (`OrderService`) not the impl class when you have one.  
2. **Final** classes / methods are hard or impossible for CGLIB to override — advice may not apply.  
3. Private methods are not advised by Spring AOP (only public calls through the proxy on Spring beans).  
4. **Self-invocation:** `this.helper()` inside the same class bypasses the proxy → no advice on `helper()`.

```text
Wrong (self-call)                 Right
─────────────────                 ─────
@Service                          @Service
class S {                         class S {
  void a(){ this.b(); }             void a(){ other.b(); } // or inject self carefully
  void b(){ ... }  // no advice     ...
}                                 }
```

***

## Topic 5 — Confirm you got a proxy

```java
@Autowired OrderService orderService;

System.out.println(orderService.getClass());
// often something like: ...$SpringCGLIB$0  or  $Proxy123
System.out.println(AopUtils.isAopProxy(orderService));
System.out.println(AopUtils.isCglibProxy(orderService));
System.out.println(AopUtils.isJdkDynamicProxy(orderService));
```

If `isAopProxy` is false, your pointcut did not match (or AOP not enabled).

## Practice lab (IDE steps)

### Step 1 — Named pointcut

Refactor last lecture’s `@Around` to use `@Pointcut` + `serviceLayer()`.

### Step 2 — Narrow the match

Change execution to only `*Service.create*(..)`.  
Confirm `get*` methods are no longer timed.

### Step 3 — Interface vs class injection

1. Extract an interface for a service.  
2. Inject the interface in the controller.  
3. Print `getClass()` and `AopUtils.isAopProxy(...)`.

### Step 4 — Self-invocation surprise

1. From method `a()`, call `this.b()` where `b` matches the pointcut.  
2. Observe advice on `b` **missing**.  
3. Move the call to another bean (or redesign) and see advice return.

### Step 5 — Final method experiment (optional)

Make a matched method `final` and see whether advice still applies with CGLIB (often breaks). Restore after learning.

***

## Short map to keep

```text
execution(...)  = main pointcut tool
@Pointcut       = name + reuse
JDK proxy       = interface-based
CGLIB proxy     = subclass-based
Proxy only sees external calls
Self-call = no advice
```

## Exercises

1. What does `..` mean inside `execution` parameter list?  
2. Why extract a named `@Pointcut`?  
3. Why might casting a proxied bean to its concrete class fail with a JDK proxy?  
4. Why does `this.b()` skip advice?  
5. How can you check at runtime that a bean is AOP-proxied?
